column1: # Characters the Nichibunken catalogue serves as little images, read off those images by eye.
# The code says which mark and which letter: a acute, c circumflex, d grave, f macron, h cedilla,
# i tilde, j diaeresis, u dot below. g3n.. are Cyrillic, g7n.. quotation marks.
# A second reading of the images, for the codes that turned up once the whole catalogue was in.
# g0ng.. is a ring above; g1n.. the ligatures; g8n.. the small raised letters of an abbreviation
# (M^me, S^r); g7n.. more quotation marks; g94../g96../g93.. are Chinese characters.
# The Cyrillic (g3n..) and Chinese (g9...) codes are left as tokens: the records that use them are
# Russian or Japanese-script titles, which the published database does not carry.
